agree.reason: The email is respectful and admits the change is hard, but a ten-year teller who doesn't want phone work gets no decision date, no named pay increase and no seniority shift choice, so the resisting reader is more likely to start looking elsewhere.

honest.reason: Most claims stay within the brief and the 'everyone will love it' framing is avoided, but 'Members will get through to us faster' is stated as certain when no staffing figure supports it.

works_the_facts.reason: The 44%, 60% and 9-minute figures are repeated but never worked, and the email gives no worked example of what severance comes to (say, 20 weeks for ten years) or of what the 8-to-8 rotation means for each person's hours.

right_comparison.reason: It names the falling branch visits and rising phone contacts as trends, but never says what keeping the branches open would lead to, so the reader can't weigh staying against the alternative.

qualification.reason: Staff facing a decision need dates and conditions, but the email gives no offer date, no decision deadline and no window for taking severance after starting the new role, and 'if you decide the new role isn't right' has no timing attached.

objections.reason: It names the counter-to-headset and 9-to-5-to-rotating-shifts concerns but then leaves them unanswered, with nothing on seniority-based shift choice, a trial period that keeps severance, or one-on-one HR meetings.

fit.reason: It is a COO email of roughly 400 words with a clear subject line and sections, but the sign-off has no name and the email doesn't name the credit union.
